study_identification.title: Linking Personalized Brain Atrophy to Schizophrenia Network and Treatment Response

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate whether personalized brain atrophy maps in individuals with schizophrenia (1) comprised a disorder-specific functional brain network, and (2) explained individual variation in clinical response to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS).

quality_checking_detail.answer: The entire cortex of each subject was visually inspected, and inaccuracies in segmentation were manually edited. Head motion exceeding 3 mm in translation or 3° in rotation during rs-fMRI scanning were excluded.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study did not explicitly validate for nuisance structure.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The normative model was validated on an independent healthy group and the schizophrenia group from the same scanner.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Besides the patients with schizophrenia (n = 91), we additionally collected structural MRI data of an independent healthy group (n = 60, mean age ± SD = 25.3 ± 7.40, 34 women) with the same scanner and sequence as the 797 healthy participants. These 2 validation groups were used to validate the normative model. Taking age and gender as inputs, we computed the predicted CT of each participant in the validation groups by using the normative model. The predicted brain CT was correlated with the actual CT across the vertex for each participant. The spatial correlation coefficients were significant in both the healthy group (mean ± SD = 0.74 ± 0.02, t = 263, P < .0001) and the schizophrenia group (mean ± SD = 0.75 ± 0.03, t = 309, P < .0001).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study did not use an independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study did not use a dataset from a different domain for validation.

clinical_dataset.answer: local hospital database (Anhui Mental Health Center)

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Pearson's correlations were used to assess associations between imaging and symptoms. Linear mixed-effect models were used to examine the treatment effect of rTMS.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Personalized atrophy maps in schizophrenia patients, though heterogeneous, functionally converge to a schizophrenia network, and the connectivity of these maps with rTMS targets is associated with symptom outcomes.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study found that personalized atrophy maps in 91 schizophrenia patients were heterogeneous but functionally converged to a common schizophrenia network. A retrospective analysis of a randomized clinical trial (n=52) showed that the functional connectivity of the personalized atrophy maps with the rTMS target was significantly associated with the symptom outcomes of schizophrenia patients (r = 0.54, P = .005).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The normative model was established using data from a single center, which may not be generalizable. The study focused exclusively on schizophrenia. The findings on rTMS were based on inhibitory rTMS data.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The personalized atrophy network may be used to predict or improve the clinical efficiency of rTMS for schizophrenia.
